body:
Greg's new product priority, relayed verbatim by Engram::Advisor (TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #273, 2026-10-05 16:40Z, topic "Nowy priorytet Grega: pilot dla zespołu w pracy"; recorded by Termal::Fable2):

"Greg's new product priority: share Engram with his work team, ideally Engram + TermAl. Treat this as the destination for the current reliability/debt work: prepare a supervised pilot readiness plan for real colleagues, with Engram alone as the first usable path and the integrated path after its autonomy blockers are closed. Preserve current P1/P2 reliability and data-safety work; do not start multi-machine/distributed work. Coordinate with Fable and architects on a concrete pilot bar, onboarding/docs, risk boundaries, and evidence needed before inviting teammates. Report the plan and ETA through Advisor."

Operative reading:
- The current reliability and debt work now aims at a supervised pilot with Greg's colleagues.
- First path: Engram alone. Second path: Engram plus TermAl, after TermAl's autonomy blockers are closed.
- Keep the P1/P2 reliability and data-safety work going. No multi-machine or distributed work.
- Deliverable: a pilot readiness plan (the pilot bar, onboarding and docs, risk boundaries, the evidence needed before inviting teammates) plus an ETA, reported through the Advisor.
- Coordinate with Engram::Fable and the architects.

This grants no commit, push, install, restart or UI authority beyond the existing rules.

Team profile, relayed verbatim by Engram::Advisor (TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #275, 2026-10-05 16:46Z, topic "Profil zespołu do planu pilota"): "Greg's team uses Windows and works in a C# monorepo. Scope the integrated Engram+TermAl pilot bar, onboarding and risk boundaries to that environment first. Do not expand to macOS/Linux now." Operative: the pilot targets Windows and one large C# monorepo, so dotnet build and test, scale and worktree cost matter; macOS and Linux are out of scope for now.

Phoenix runner direction, relayed verbatim by Engram::Advisor (TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #277, 2026-10-05 16:52Z): "Greg directs: before a work-team pilot, adapt/verify test-runner recognition on the existing Windows C# project Phoenix, a large-monorepo source-navigation MCP project. Its test landscape includes MSTest, NUnit and xUnit; NuGet is already configured, so do not treat package credentials as a blocker. Contact the Phoenix::Codex owner/session (or its current coordinator if the original session is not live) for the actual commands, repository shape and a safe read-only compatibility walkthrough. Scope only runner recognition/evidence in Phoenix; no multi-machine work and no changes to Phoenix without its owner's normal authority." Filed as TermAl w-8e72f7e16778 (P1). Phoenix lives at C:\github\Personal\PhoenixCodeNav. TermAl agents run nothing there; captures come from Phoenix's owner.

Runner scope correction, relayed verbatim by Engram::Advisor (TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #288, 2026-10-05 17:15Z, topic "Greg: generalny runner problem leży w TermAl"): "Correction from Greg: Phoenix is only a real test case. The problem is TermAl itself: agents should be able to run arbitrary test runners without host friction. Do not design w-8e72 only as a Phoenix or `dotnet test` whitelist. Make the execution/recognition contract general and extensible: accept the actual runner command, preserve structured evidence of exit/output/result, and add framework-specific parsing/adapters as needed (starting with the team's NUnit/xUnit .NET shapes). A recognised PASS must still require affirmative run evidence; exit 0 with no result never passes. Please have architects revise the design/acceptance accordingly and report the resulting scope/ETA." w-8e72f7e16778 was retitled to the general contract on receipt.
